messages:
Ivy N: bringing up titan-lite (int4) canary; used parse_granularity="line" to trade for latency but seeing nested funcall args where a trailing comma at a chunk boundary gets dropped and strict linter rejects the whole call :confused:
Liam G: can you paste the exact streaming chunk sequence that fails?
Ivy N: snippet:
chunk A: ..."tool_call":{"name":"get_profile","args":"{\"id\":\"u-9\",\"prefs\":{\"email\":true,\"sms\":false,"
chunk B: \"notifications\":\"daily\"}}"...
Noah R: so the comma between prefs and notifications got eaten at the boundary. our repair heuristics that only append closers won't add commas, so they still fail. this is different from missing closers.
Olivia C: options: (a) conservative: detect missing separators at chunk joins and try to reinsert comma if adjacent tokens look like close/open pairs, but only when schema expects an array/object separator; (b) fallback: switch granularity to "block" for this model; (c) improve streaming delimiter so we never split inside inner JSON.
Liam G: (a) risks inventing separators incorrectly. we need a validation step: only insert comma if repaired string validates against schema and insertion is minimal. add unit tests with negative cases where inserting a comma would create a new field or change types.
watchdog-bot: canary snapshot: line mode parse_fail=0.41% p50=140ms p95=360ms; block mode parse_fail=0.12% p50=200ms p95=470ms
Ivy N: proposal: prototype an opt-in "separator_heal: conservative" that attempts to insert a comma at a chunk boundary only when counts of braces/brackets are balanced after insertion and strict schema validator accepts. gate behind 1% canary and collect schema_violation metric.
Noah R: i'll draft tests for boundary-comma positive and negative cases. also add replay trace cb-titan-1777 for QA.
Olivia C: i'll coordinate infra flip and dashboard collection if PR lands. pin rollout to 1% and stop if schema_violation increases >0.05%.
Ivy N: action items: Liam implement conservative separator_heal, Noah tests & replay, Olivia canary run. tagging security for logging review. thanks!
